intended_object: Currying of a multilinear map f in n+1 variables at position p: the linear map x ↦ (m ↦ f(m with x inserted at position p)), from M p to multilinear maps in the remaining n variables (indexed via p.succAbove). Inferred from the docstring and from its role as the generalisation of curryLeft (p = 0).
explanation: The body sends x to mk' (fun m ↦ f (p.insertNth x m)). `insertNth` places x at slot p and fills the other slots with m in order, which is exactly currying in the p-th variable. For fixed x the map is multilinear in m because f is. It is linear in x by map_insertNth_add and map_insertNth_smul. It is a two-sided inverse of LinearMap.uncurryMid (proved in the file) and is packaged as curryMidLinearEquiv, which is the same map as a linear equivalence rather than a separate counterpart. The generality matches the sibling definitions curryLeft and curryRight: any commutative semiring and arbitrary modules. Indexing by Fin (n+1) is inherent to the construction, since succAbove and insertNth are needed to present the remaining variables as an n-tuple. A version for an arbitrary index type would be a different construction (over the subtype {j // j ≠ i}), and Mathlib has no such construction. There are no degenerate-case problems: for n = 0 the target is multilinear maps in zero variables, which is correct.
